package_info.why_malicious: The package is designed to exfiltrate highly sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, Windows SAM and SYSTEM hives, and Amazon EC2 credentials) to an external attacker-controlled endpoint, indicating clear intent to steal credentials and compromise systems.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when index.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of /etc/passwd, reads its contents, encodes it in base64, and stores it for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing /etc/passwd is unnecessary for normal package operation and is a common indicator of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not access or exfiltrate sensitive system files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administration tools may read /etc/passwd for legitimate auditing, but not in a general-purpose npm package.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of the Windows SAM file, reads its contents, encodes it in base64, and stores it for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the Windows SAM file is a clear attempt to steal password hashes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should never access Windows credential stores.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic or backup tools may access SAM, but not general packages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of the Windows SYSTEM hive, reads its contents, encodes it in base64, and stores it for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the SYSTEM hive is a known technique for extracting system secrets.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not access or exfiltrate SYSTEM hives.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic tools may access SYSTEM hive, but not npm packages.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code prepares to access the AWS EC2 instance metadata service to retrieve security credentials for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the EC2 metadata service is a common cloud credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not access cloud instance metadata.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud management agents may access metadata, but not general npm packages.

try:

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code sends a notification to a Discord webhook, then executes an encrypted (base64) payload that exfiltrates data and opens a reverse shell to a remote IP.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should not contact external webhooks or execute encrypted payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py is expected to handle installation, not exfiltrate data or open shells.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; encrypted payloads and webhooks in setup.py are always suspicious.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or imported, triggering execution of index.js (npm) or setup.py (PyPI).
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive files and credentials.

attack_chain.action: Sensitive files (/etc/passwd, SAM, SYSTEM) and cloud credentials are read and encoded.
Data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints (Discord webhook, external server).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to credentials and potentially remote shell.

attack_chain.action: Reverse shell is opened, allowing attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands.

behavioral_signatures: Access to /etc/passwd, Windows SAM, or SYSTEM files by npm/PyPI packages
Base64 encoding of sensitive file contents
Outbound HTTP POST to Discord webhooks or other external endpoints
Execution of encrypted (base64) payloads in setup.py
file_indicators: References to Discord webhook URLs in package code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package installation or import events where code accesses sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM), encodes data in base64, or makes outbound network requests to known exfiltration endpoints (Discord webhooks, AWS metadata service). Flag any setup.py or index.js files containing encrypted payloads or references to credential stores. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected connections to Discord, AWS metadata IPs, or other suspicious domains during package installation or runtime.
